# Skill: doc-entrypoint-template

## Purpose

Canonical template and structure rules for the single documentation entrypoint (`OUTPUT_PATH/ENTRYPOINT`, default `OUTPUT_PATH/SUMMARY.md`).
Load this skill when generating the entrypoint (executor Phase N+2) or when navigating documentation (search-doc).

---

## Entrypoint Rules

- There is exactly **one** entrypoint file per documentation project.
- Its path is `OUTPUT_PATH/ENTRYPOINT` (read both values from `.github/prompts.config`).
- Default path: `OUTPUT_PATH/SUMMARY.md`
- Do **not** create additional index or navigation files alongside it.
- The file must serve both human readers and AI agents (e.g., `search-doc`).

---

## Required Sections

The entrypoint must contain all of the following sections, in this order:

| # | Section | Purpose |
|---|---------|---------|
| 1 | **Start Here** | Short orientation — how to use this file |
| 2 | **Documentation Structure** | Explains the top-level folder layout |
| 3 | **Pages (Course Order)** | Every document in pedagogical reading order |
| 4 | **By Domain** | All documents grouped by domain folder |
| 5 | **Pages (A–Z)** | Every document sorted A–Z by title |
| 6 | **Topic Index (A–Z)** | Every unique topic → list of documents |
| 7 | **Search Tips for AI Agents** | Navigation strategy and metadata usage |
| 8 | **Project Overview** | Aggregate counts |
| 9 | **Source File Mapping** | Source transcript → generated document table |
| 10 | **Documentation Standards** | Brief summary of structural conventions |
| 11 | **Generation Information** | Agent, date, config, paths |

---

## Full Template

```markdown
# [PROJECT_NAME]

## Start Here

- Read this file top-to-bottom to discover the documentation.
- For folder navigation, open each folder's `overview.md` (when enabled).

---

## Documentation Structure

- Top-level folders under `OUTPUT_PATH/` are domains (`DOMAINS[].path`).
- Inside each domain: topic/subtopic folders and documents.
- See the folder tree in the **By Domain** section below.

---

## Pages (Course Order)

List EVERY generated document in pedagogical order (prerequisites before advanced topics).
For each entry:

- `[Document Title](relative/path/to/doc.md)` — Topics: Topic A, Topic B — _One-line description._

---

## By Domain

For each domain folder, list:

### [Domain Name] (`DOMAINS[].path/`)

- [`overview.md`](domain-path/overview.md) — Domain overview
- [`01_TopicDoc.md`](domain-path/01_TopicDoc.md) — Topics: Topic A — _Description._

---

## Pages (A–Z)

List EVERY generated document sorted A–Z by title. Each entry must include its topics.

- [`Document Title`](relative/path.md) — Topics: Topic A, Topic B

---

## Topic Index (A–Z)

List EVERY unique topic sorted A–Z. For each topic, list all documents that contain it.

**Topic A**
- [`Document Title`](relative/path.md)
- [`Another Document`](relative/path2.md)

**Topic B**
- [`Document Title`](relative/path.md)

---

## Search Tips for AI Agents

### Recommended Search Strategies

**By Domain**:
- Start with the domain `overview.md`
- Navigate: domain overview → topic overviews → documents

**By Topic**:
- Use the Topic Index (A–Z) above
- Follow each page's `related` links

**By Reading Order**:
- Use Pages (Course Order) for structured learning
- Prerequisites appear before advanced topics

### Metadata Usage

Every document includes:

- **Topics**: keywords for semantic search
- **Related**: direct links to connected documents
- **Sources**: original transcript file paths for traceability

---

## Project Overview

- **Total documents**: [N]
- **Domains covered**: [N]
- **Unique topics**: [N]
- **Cross-references**: [N]
- **Source files processed**: [N]

---

## Source File Mapping

**Purpose**: Trace generated documentation back to original sources.

| Source File | Generated Document | Domain | Topics |
|-------------|-------------------|--------|--------|
| `transcripts/clean/[domain]/[file].md` | `[output-path]/[doc].md` | [Domain] | [topics] |

---

## Documentation Standards

- **Structure**: 2–4 heading levels maximum
- **Metadata**: per `METADATA_FORMAT` from `.github/prompts.config`
- **Links**: relative paths for portability
- **Language**: [LANGUAGE from config]

---

## Generation Information

- **Generated by**: [AGENT_NAME]
- **Generation date**: [FULL DATE and TIME]
- **Configuration**: `.github/prompts.config`
- **Source transcripts**: [SOURCE_PATHS]
- **Output location**: [OUTPUT_PATH]
```

---

## Folder Overview Template (`overview.md`)

Each folder node (domain folder, topic folder) must contain a file named `OVERVIEW_FILE_NAME` (default `overview.md`) with the following structure:

```markdown
---
title: "[Folder Name] Overview"
topics:
  - Topic A
  - Topic B
generated_at: "2026-03-30T10:00:00Z"
doc_type: overview
---

# [Folder Name]

**Topics**: Topic A, Topic B
**Doc type**: overview
**Generated at**: 2026-03-30T10:00:00Z

## What This Section Covers

[Brief paragraph describing what the folder contains and who it is for.]

## Contents

- [`01_TopicDoc.md`](01_TopicDoc.md) — _One-line description._
- [`02_AnotherDoc.md`](02_AnotherDoc.md) — _One-line description._
- [`subfolder/`](subfolder/overview.md) — _Sub-section description._
```

---

## Entrypoint Validation Checklist

- [ ] File exists at `OUTPUT_PATH/ENTRYPOINT`
- [ ] All 11 required sections are present
- [ ] Every generated document appears in both **Pages (Course Order)** and **Pages (A–Z)**
- [ ] Topic Index is exhaustive — every topic from every document is listed
- [ ] Source File Mapping covers every generated document
- [ ] All links are valid relative paths from `OUTPUT_PATH/`
- [ ] No broken links (all link targets exist on disk)
- [ ] Project Overview counts match actual file counts

## How `search-doc` Uses the Entrypoint

1. Reads `OUTPUT_PATH/ENTRYPOINT` as the primary search index.
2. Uses **Topic Index (A–Z)** to locate candidate pages for a given topic.
3. Uses **Pages (Course Order)** to understand prerequisite relationships.
4. Uses **Source File Mapping** to identify transcripts when documentation is insufficient.
5. Follows **Search Tips for AI Agents** for multi-step discovery.
